title: Java fundamentals — Beginner
description: 64 focused Java 17 questions: practical repairs and five attributed imports.
subject: Java fundamentals

tests.title: Getting a program running
tests.description: Correct common Java mistakes using choices about the same concept.

questions.prompt: `java Hello` reports that no main method was found. Hello is intended to be a Java 17 console application. What needs to be added?
questions.explanation: Program entry point: main is the conventional launcher entry method. Add a suitable main method to the launched class. Example: public static void main(String[] args).
options: make the class abstract so the launcher supplies main
add a constructor named main
add a suitable main method to the launched class
rename any method to start

questions.prompt: A Java source file is saved as Hello.txt. Which change makes its filename suitable for the usual javac source-file workflow?
questions.explanation: Source file extension: Java source files normally use the .java extension. Save Java source with a .java extension. Example: Save a public Hello class in Hello.java.
options: change the class name to Hello.txt
save Java source with a .java extension
rename the source to Hello.class without compiling it
save only Hello.jar as plain source text

questions.prompt: Welcome.java declares `public class Hello`. What fixes the public-class filename mismatch?
questions.explanation: Public class filename: a public top-level class must match its source filename. Rename the file or the public class to match. Example: public class Hello in Hello.java.
options: add a second public class named Welcome to the same file
rename the file or the public class to match
make the constructor name match Welcome while leaving the class Hello
add an import for Welcome

questions.prompt: `javac src/Hello.java` reports that the source file does not exist. The file is actually in app/Hello.java. What should the command use?
questions.explanation: Compilation: javac compiles source into class files. Supply the correct source file path to javac. Example: javac Hello.java.
options: supply the correct source file path to javac
use java on the same missing path
rename the missing output class without supplying source
remove the .java extension from the missing path

questions.prompt: Hello.class has already been compiled in the current directory, and no Hello.java source is available. How should it be launched from that directory?
questions.explanation: Running a class: java launches a compiled class by its class name. Launch the compiled class by name. Example: java Hello.
options: launch the compiled class by name
launch Hello.class as the class name
supply javac as the application class
rename the compiled class file to Hello.java

questions.prompt: The declaration `int count = 1` appears inside a method without a terminator. Which correction completes this declaration statement?
questions.explanation: Statements: a simple Java statement commonly ends with a semicolon. End the declaration statement with a semicolon. Example: int count = 1;.
options: use an empty comment in place of the terminator
end the declaration statement with a semicolon
end the declaration with a colon
put a comma after the declaration

questions.prompt: An if block opens with `{` but never closes before the surrounding method ends. What fixes the unmatched block?
questions.explanation: Blocks: braces group statements into a block. Close the block with a matching brace. Example: if (ready) { start(); }.
options: indent the last statement to close the block
close the block with a matching brace
add another opening brace at the end
replace the missing brace with a semicolon

questions.prompt: In `// count++;`, the increment never executes. What must change to make it executable code?
questions.explanation: Line comments: two slashes begin a comment to the end of the line. Put executable code on an uncommented line. Example: // explain the next step.
options: indent the text after // to make it executable
use uppercase letters after // to end the comment
put executable code on an uncommented line
add a semicolon after the commented text to execute it

questions.prompt: A `/*` comment accidentally includes the rest of the source file. How should the intended comment be closed?
questions.explanation: Block comments: slash-star and star-slash delimit a block comment. Close the comment with */. Example: /* explanation */.
options: close the comment with a brace
insert a newline to end every block comment
close the comment with */
close the comment with //

questions.prompt: Why must `int 2item = 4;` be changed, and which naming rule should the replacement follow?
questions.explanation: Identifiers: a variable name cannot start with a digit. Choose an identifier that does not start with a digit. Example: int item2 = 4;.
options: declare 2item final to allow the leading digit
choose an identifier that does not start with a digit
put quotes around 2item to make it an identifier
import a variable named 2item

tests.title: Names and values
tests.description: Correct common Java mistakes using choices about the same concept.

questions.prompt: A method declares count but later reads Count. How should the unresolved name be corrected?
questions.explanation: Case sensitivity: Java treats names with different letter case as distinct. Use the exact declared capitalization. Example: count and Count are different names.
options: add final to make names case-insensitive
capitalize all uses without changing the declaration
add an import to alias Count to count
use the exact declared capitalization

questions.prompt: A method tries to assign to age, but no local, parameter, or field named age exists. What must be added before use?
questions.explanation: Variable declaration: a variable declaration gives a type and a name. Declare age with a suitable type before use. Example: int age;.
options: declare age with a suitable type before use
use age first so Java infers its type from the later call
add parentheses around the undeclared name
write age as a comment before using it

questions.prompt: `int age; System.out.print(age);` appears inside a method. What is required before the print statement?
questions.explanation: Local initialization: a local variable must be assigned before its value is read. Assign the local variable before reading it. Example: int age = 20; print(age);.
options: rely on every local int starting at zero
mark the unassigned local final and read it
add an import to initialize the local automatically
assign the local variable before reading it

questions.prompt: `int price = 12.75;` does not compile. Which type or conversion decision is required for the fractional value?
questions.explanation: Integer type: int stores a signed 32-bit integer. Choose a suitable floating-point type or convert explicitly. Example: int count = 12;.
options: append f while leaving the variable int
put the fraction in quotes and assign it to int
declare the int final to permit fractional values
choose a suitable floating-point type or convert explicitly

questions.prompt: `long size = 3000000000;` fails because the unsuffixed literal is out of range. How should the exact long literal be written?
questions.explanation: Long literals: an L suffix makes an integer literal long. Add L to the long literal. Example: long size = 3000000000L;.
options: cast the already out-of-range unsuffixed literal to long
put the digits in quotes and assign the String directly to long
add L to the long literal
append f to preserve the exact integer as a long literal

questions.prompt: `float rate = 1.5;` fails with a possible loss of precision. Which correction fits Java's literal typing rules?
questions.explanation: Floating-point default: a decimal floating-point literal is double by default. Use 1.5f or a double variable. Example: double price = 1.5;.
options: append L to the decimal literal
make the float variable final without changing the literal
use 1.5f or a double variable
leave 1.5 unchanged because every decimal literal is float

questions.prompt: `boolean ready = "true";` does not compile. Which value belongs on the right side for a true boolean?
questions.explanation: Boolean values: boolean has true and false values. Use the boolean literal true. Example: boolean ready = true;.
options: use the boolean literal true
cast the String directly to boolean
use the integer 1 as a boolean literal
remove quotes and use yes as a built-in boolean literal

questions.prompt: `char grade = "A";` does not compile. How should the single character literal be delimited?
questions.explanation: Character literals: a char literal uses single quotes. Use single quotes for one character. Example: char grade = 'A';.
options: use single quotes for one character
keep double quotes and make the char final
add a second character inside single quotes
use a String cast as an automatic char conversion

questions.prompt: `String name = 'Ada';` uses invalid literal syntax. What should delimit the text?
questions.explanation: String literals: a String literal uses double quotes. Use double quotes for a String. Example: String name = "Ada";.
options: use double quotes for a String
keep multiple characters in single quotes
use backticks as Java String delimiters
omit all delimiters so the words become a literal

tests.title: Operators
tests.description: Correct common Java mistakes using choices about the same concept.

questions.prompt: A greeting and a name are both Strings. Which use of plus correctly combines their text?
questions.explanation: String concatenation: plus joins strings into a new String. Use plus to concatenate textual values. Example: "Hi " + name.
options: use plus to concatenate textual values
cast the combined String directly to int
use == to add two numeric Strings
use multiplication to concatenate instead of plus

questions.prompt: `count == 3;` was intended to store 3 in count. Which operator should be used for that update?
questions.explanation: Assignment: one equals sign assigns a value. Use = for assignment. Example: count = 3;.
options: use = for assignment
use === to assign the new value
reverse == to =! for assignment
add parentheses around the equality comparison to make it assign

questions.prompt: `if (count = 3)` does not compare count with 3. Which change produces the intended primitive equality test?
questions.explanation: Equality comparison: two equals signs compare primitive values. Use == for the primitive comparison. Example: count == 3.
options: use == for the primitive comparison
use = and rely on automatic boolean conversion
use === for primitive equality in Java
use != when testing whether both values are the same

questions.prompt: `count =! 0` was intended to test whether count differs from zero. Which operator is required?
questions.explanation: Not equal comparison: != tests whether values differ. Use != for inequality. Example: count != 0.
options: use <> as the Java inequality operator
put spaces inside =! to make it valid
replace the comparison with assignment
use != for inequality

questions.prompt: A condition must be true only when ready and valid are true, and valid must not be evaluated when ready is false. Which operator fits?
questions.explanation: Logical AND: && requires both boolean operands to be true. Use && for short-circuit boolean AND. Example: ready && valid.
options: use ! on the right operand to create short-circuit AND
use && for short-circuit boolean AND
keep & because it skips the right operand when the left is false
use logical OR to require both operands to be true

questions.prompt: A fallback condition must be evaluated only when the first condition is false. Which boolean OR operator provides that behavior?
questions.explanation: Logical OR: the logical OR operator succeeds when either boolean operand is true. Use the double-pipe operator for short-circuit boolean OR. Example: a condition is true when ready or retry is true.
options: use && so either operand can make the result true
keep the single pipe because it always skips an unnecessary right operand
add ! to both operands instead of using OR
use the double-pipe operator for short-circuit boolean OR

questions.prompt: ready is a boolean. What should replace the invalid expression `not ready` to reverse its value?
questions.explanation: Logical NOT: ! reverses a boolean value. Use ! before the boolean expression. Example: !ready.
options: use ! before the boolean expression
write NOT as an uppercase keyword
use ~ on the boolean expression
compare the boolean to the integer zero

questions.prompt: The expression `7 / 3` produces a quotient, but the program needs the remainder. Which operator should replace division?
questions.explanation: Remainder: % returns the remainder of integer division. Use the % operator. Example: 7 % 3 gives 1.
options: use the % operator
use / and keep the quotient
use // as the remainder operator
use %% as a separate Java operator

questions.prompt: `double average = 7 / 2;` stores 3.0. How can the division itself produce 3.5?
questions.explanation: Integer division: division of two ints discards the fractional part. Convert an operand to a floating-point type first. Example: 7 / 2 gives 3.
options: append a decimal point to the variable name
convert an operand to a floating-point type first
cast the integer result to double only after dividing
store the int division result in a double and expect the fraction back

questions.prompt: count starts at 4. The statement `count++;` leaves it at 5, but the intended result was 6. Which correction matches the required step?
questions.explanation: Increment: ++ increases a numeric variable by one. Use ++ for one step or += 2 for two. Example: count++;.
options: make the variable final before incrementing it
use ++ for one step or += 2 for two
apply ++ twice and expect only one increment
replace ++ with -- to increase the value

tests.title: Control flow
tests.description: Correct common Java mistakes using choices about the same concept.

questions.prompt: `count + 2;` neither forms a valid standalone Java expression statement nor stores the sum. Which change updates count?
questions.explanation: Compound assignment: += adds and assigns in one expression. Assign the result or use +=. Example: count += 2;.
options: leave count + 2 as a standalone Java expression statement
use count == count + 2 to store the sum
make count final so addition updates it automatically
assign the result or use +=

questions.prompt: `if (count)` uses an int as a condition. What must replace count in the condition?
questions.explanation: If statement: if executes a branch when its condition is true. Write a boolean expression in the condition. Example: if (ready) { start(); }.
options: surround the int with extra parentheses to make it boolean
write a boolean expression in the condition
use a nonzero int because Java treats it as true
cast the int directly to boolean

questions.prompt: An alternate action should run only when ready is false in an if/else pair. Where should that action go?
questions.explanation: Else branch: else runs when the paired if condition is false. Put the alternate action in else. Example: if (ready) start(); else waitForReady();.
options: use else without a matching if to run after every condition
put the alternate action in else
put the alternate action inside the true branch
add another else to force both branches to run

questions.prompt: Several independent conditions may be true, and every matching action must run. An else-if chain runs only the first match. What structure is needed?
questions.explanation: Else-if chain: else if checks another condition after earlier conditions fail. Use separate if statements when all checks must run. Example: if (score > 90) a(); else if (score > 80) b();.
options: add braces around the same else-if chain to run every branch
replace all conditions with assignment expressions
use separate if statements when all checks must run
raise the first matching threshold so every later else-if executes

questions.prompt: A for loop's counter never changes, so its true condition never becomes false. Where should the required counter update be supplied?
questions.explanation: For loop: for combines initialization, condition, and update. Update the counter in the loop. Example: for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) { work(); }.
options: make the counter final so it advances automatically
add a semicolon immediately after the loop header to increment it
move the counter declaration outside the loop without ever updating it
update the counter in the loop

questions.prompt: A loop body must run once even when its initial continuation condition is false. Which loop form meets that requirement?
questions.explanation: While loop: while checks its condition before each iteration. Use do-while if one execution is required. Example: while (ready) { work(); }.
options: add braces to guarantee one iteration even when false
initialize the condition to false to force the first iteration
place a semicolon after while so the body runs exactly once as part of the loop
use do-while if one execution is required

questions.prompt: A do-while body runs once with an initially false condition, but zero iterations are required in that case. Which loop form should be used?
questions.explanation: Do-while loop: do-while checks its condition after the body. Use while when the body should possibly be skipped. Example: do { read(); } while (retry);.
options: add braces to skip the first body execution
put false in the trailing condition to prevent all body executions
use continue before the condition to undo the first iteration
use while when the body should possibly be skipped

questions.prompt: An unlabeled break inside nested loops exits only the inner loop. What is needed to also leave the outer loop?
questions.explanation: Break statement: break exits the nearest loop or switch. Use explicit control flow for outer loops. Example: if (done) break;.
options: use continue to exit all enclosing loops
indent break under the outer loop to change its target
use explicit control flow for outer loops
add a second break after the first unconditional break

questions.prompt: Finding a target should end the loop, but continue merely advances to another iteration. Which statement matches the intended behavior?
questions.explanation: Continue statement: continue skips to the next loop iteration. Use break to exit the loop. Example: if (skip) continue;.
options: add another continue immediately afterward
use return to exit only the current iteration while keeping the method running
use a semicolon after continue to terminate the whole loop
use break to exit the loop

questions.prompt: scores must refer to an int array, but `int scores;` declares a scalar. What must be included in its declaration?
questions.explanation: Array declaration: an array variable names an array type. Declare the variable with []. Example: int[] scores;.
options: declare the variable with []
declare int scores and rely on later indexing to turn it into an array
use angle brackets int<scores>
declare array int scores without square brackets

tests.title: Arrays and methods
tests.description: Correct common Java mistakes using choices about the same concept.

questions.prompt: An int array is full, and writing at its length index fails. What storage change is needed to support more elements?
questions.explanation: Array creation: new creates an array with a fixed length. Create an array of the needed size or use a list. Example: int[] scores = new int[3];.
options: create an array of the needed size or use a list
write to scores[scores.length] to append automatically
increase scores.length with ++
cast scores to a longer array without allocating one

questions.prompt: The program reads `scores[1]` but needs the first element of a nonempty Java array. Which index should it use?
questions.explanation: Array indexing: array indexes start at zero. Use index 0 for the first element. Example: scores[0] accesses the first element.
options: use index -1 for the first element
use the length as the first valid index
use index 0 for the first element
use index 1 because Java arrays are one-based

questions.prompt: `scores.length()` fails when scores is an int array. How should its element count be accessed?
questions.explanation: Array length: an array exposes its length through a field. Read the length field without parentheses. Example: scores.length.
options: keep length() because every array field is a method
use size() because all arrays implement List
subtract one from the last index to get every array length
read the length field without parentheses

questions.prompt: In `for (int score : scores)`, score is an element value. The algorithm also needs each position. Which loop approach should be used?
questions.explanation: Enhanced for loop: an enhanced for loop visits elements in sequence. Use an indexed loop when an index is needed. Example: for (int score : scores) { print(score); }.
options: use the element value as an index for every array
increment the enhanced-for variable to make the array longer
assign to the loop variable to replace every primitive array element
use an indexed loop when an index is needed

questions.prompt: `int twice(int n) { int result = n * 2; }` computes a value but has no return. What must the method supply?
questions.explanation: Method declaration: a method declares return type, name, and parameters. Return a value of the declared type. Example: int twice(int n) { return n * 2; }.
options: change the method name to the return type
add a semicolon after the body to return automatically
rely on an implicit zero result from every non-void method
return a value of the declared type

questions.prompt: A caller tries `int result = greet();`, but greet returns void. What must the API provide if this call should produce an int result?
questions.explanation: Void method: void marks a method with no result value. Use a return type when a value is required. Example: void greet() { print("Hi"); }.
options: use a return type when a value is required
cast the void result to int
assign the void call to an Integer instead
make the method public so its void call produces a value

questions.prompt: `int twice(int n)` requires a parameter, but the caller writes twice(). What must the invocation supply?
questions.explanation: Method argument: an argument supplies a value to a parameter. Pass an int argument. Example: twice(4).
options: pass an int argument
call twice() because missing int arguments default to zero
put the int value after the call's closing parenthesis
declare the result variable final to supply the argument

questions.prompt: A required update appears immediately after an unconditional return in the same block. Where should that update be moved?
questions.explanation: Return statement: return ends a method invocation and can supply its result. Place needed work before return. Example: return count;.
options: put needed work immediately after return in the same block
make the method static so execution continues after return
place needed work before return
add another return after the unconditional return

questions.prompt: A variable declared inside an if block is needed by later code outside that block. Where should its declaration be placed if both uses must share it?
questions.explanation: Scope: a local variable is visible only inside its declared scope. Declare shared state in an enclosing scope when appropriate. Example: int x inside a method block.
options: declare shared state in an enclosing scope when appropriate
indent the later use into the old scope without changing braces
mark the block-local variable final to extend its visibility
add an import for the local variable

questions.prompt: `String name = null; name.length();` fails at runtime. What is needed before this method invocation can succeed?
questions.explanation: Null reference: null denotes no object reference. Assign a non-null String before invoking a method. Example: String name = null;.
options: compare the null reference to an empty String using its instance equals method
assign a non-null String before invoking a method
cast null to String so method calls succeed
call length first and check for null afterward

tests.title: Strings and program structure
tests.description: Correct common Java mistakes using choices about the same concept.

questions.prompt: `text.length` fails when text is a String. How should its length be read?
questions.explanation: String length: String.length() returns the number of UTF-16 code units. Call the length() method on a String. Example: "cat".length() gives 3.
options: call the length() method on a String
read text.length as though String were an array
read text.size without calling a method
use text.capacity() as a String method

questions.prompt: Two separately created Strings contain the same text, but == reports false. Which comparison expresses equality of their contents?
questions.explanation: String equality: String.equals compares String contents. Use equals for content equality. Example: "cat".equals(name).
options: use = to compare String values
call hashCode and assume equal hashes guarantee equal text
use equals for content equality
use == because it always compares character sequences

questions.prompt: Calling `name.trim();` leaves name referring to the original String. How should the trimmed result be used?
questions.explanation: String immutability: a String operation does not modify the existing String. Store or use the returned String. Example: name = name.trim();.
options: call trim repeatedly until the original String mutates
assign the result of length() back to the same String variable
store or use the returned String
mark name final so trim modifies the original String

questions.prompt: The program receives the text "42" and needs its numeric int value. Which conversion should be performed?
questions.explanation: Parsing an integer: Integer.parseInt converts decimal text to int. Parse the text as an integer. Example: Integer.parseInt("42").
options: remove the quotes at runtime by subtracting an empty String
assign the String to Integer using automatic unboxing
parse the text as an integer
cast the String object directly to int

questions.prompt: Parsing invalid decimal input may throw NumberFormatException. Where should recovery for that failure be placed?
questions.explanation: Try-catch: catch handles a matching thrown exception. Put recovery in the matching catch path. Example: try { parse(); } catch (NumberFormatException e) { recover(); }.
options: expect catch to execute once on every successful call
put an unconditional return before try so catch runs
use finally instead of catch to identify only NumberFormatException
put recovery in the matching catch path

questions.prompt: Cleanup is needed whether a try block completes normally or throws. Which purpose should the finally block serve?
questions.explanation: Finally block: finally runs after try or catch during normal completion or exception propagation. Use finally for cleanup. Example: finally { close(); }.
options: assume a matching catch always replaces the need for cleanup
use finally for cleanup
return every success result from finally even when it suppresses a failure
put cleanup after a return in the same try block

questions.prompt: A class declares `package example.app;`, but other code treats it as being in the unnamed package. What must references account for?
questions.explanation: Package declaration: package gives a source file its package name. Use the declared package when referencing the class. Example: package example.app;.
options: import the package as though it were an object instance
remove dots from the qualified class name without moving the type
use the declared package when referencing the class
ignore the declaration because folder names always override it

questions.prompt: `import java.util.List;` makes the type name available but no list object exists. What additional action is needed to use an instance?
questions.explanation: Import declaration: import lets source use a type's simple name. Create or obtain an object separately from importing its type. Example: import java.util.List;.
options: expect the import to allocate one object per use
use import instead of new to choose a list implementation
create or obtain an object separately from importing its type
call a constructor by writing an import inside a method

questions.prompt: A static import is expected to create a Math object. What does the import actually allow instead?
questions.explanation: Static import: static import allows unqualified access to a static member. Use static import only for static members. Example: import static java.lang.Math.PI;.
options: use static import only for static members
use static import to construct the declaring class
import an instance field statically without an object
write a constructor call in the static import declaration

questions.prompt: `var name;` has no initializer. What must be supplied so Java can infer the local variable's type?
questions.explanation: Type inference with var: var infers a local variable's static type from its initializer. Initialize a var local variable in its declaration. Example: var name = "Ada";.
options: use var for a method parameter in an ordinary named method
initialize a var local variable in its declaration
assign null alone and expect a useful inferred class type
declare var as a field without a type or initializer

questions.prompt: What does the 'compareTo()' method return when two strings are equal?
questions.explanation: String.compareTo returns zero when the strings have the same character sequence; negative and positive results indicate lexicographic ordering.
options: True

questions.prompt: Which of these is not a primitive data type in Java?
questions.explanation: String is a class, so String values are references. int, char, and boolean are primitive types.
options: int
char
boolean
String

questions.prompt: Which operator is used for bitwise AND in Java?
questions.explanation: For integral operands, & computes bitwise AND. The other choices are bitwise OR, XOR, and complement, respectively.

questions.prompt: What is the range of byte data type in Java?
questions.explanation: byte is an 8-bit signed two's-complement integer, with values from -128 through 127.

questions.prompt: Which of these methods is used to get the size of a List in Java?
questions.explanation: List exposes its element count through size(). Arrays instead have a length field; String has a length() method.
options: length()
getSize()
size()
length
